Colour palettes for surface maps

Source: R/render_surface_rgba.R
surface_palette.Rd

The palettes neurosurf uses for statistical surface maps, as colour vectors for any renderer: render_surface_rgba and surface_figure use them by default, and they can be passed to view_surface (cmap) or surface_layer (colormap) so interactive and static figures share one colour language. The two-sided palette runs from dark blue through light blue and light orange to dark red. It has no white or grey centre, so values just past a threshold stay distinct from the grey anatomy.

Usage

surface_palette(
  type = c("two_sided", "positive", "negative"),
  n = 256L,
  limits = NULL,
  threshold = NULL
)

Arguments

type

"two_sided" for signed maps, "positive" or "negative" for one-tailed maps.

n

Number of colours. NULL returns the palette's anchor colours.

limits, threshold

Optional colour limits and threshold magnitude. With both, the result is the lookup table the CPU renderer uses: n colours evenly spaced over limits, with each tail's ramp starting at the threshold. Pass it with the same limits to a viewer (for example surface_layer) to reproduce a static figure's colours exactly.

Value

A character vector of hex colours.

Examples

surface_palette("two_sided", n = 7)
#> [1] "#12397B" "#2A64AB" "#5B92CF" "#BF9BA1" "#E47553" "#C0352C" "#790A1F"
surface_palette("positive")
